content: The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of various drugs. The following are detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration of specific drugs with CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, particularly focusing on cobicistat and atazanavir: 1. Cobicistat and Levomilnacipran: Cobicistat increases the plasma levels and effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, do not exceed a daily dose of 80 mg of levomilnacipran. 2. Cobicistat and Levonorgestrel (Intrauterine): Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Atazanavir and Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Bisglycinate: Atazanavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a non-hormonal contraceptive method instead. 4. Cobicistat and Lomitapide: Cobicistat increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Lopinavir and Atazanavir: Lopinavir increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lorlatinib and Cobicistat: Lorlatinib decreases cobicistat levels, while cobicistat increases lorlatinib levels via CYP3A4 interactions. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, return to the previous lorlatinib dose after three plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 7. Atazanavir and Lovotibeglogene Autotemcel: Discontinue antiretroviral therapy (ART) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period due to potential interference with manufacturing. 8. Cobicistat and Lurbinectedin: Cobicistat increases lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous lurbinectedin dose. 9. Atazanavir and Macitentan: Atazanavir increases macitentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Magnesium Oxide and Atazanavir: Magnesium oxide increases gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Administer atazanavir two hours before or one hour after magnesium oxide. 11. Atazanavir and Mefloquine: Atazanavir increases mefloquine levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Cobicistat and Midazolam (Intranasal): Cobicistat increases midazolam levels, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Atazanavir and Midazolam: Atazanavir increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Cobicistat and Midostaurin: Cobicistat increases midostaurin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 15. Mitotane and Cobicistat: Mitotane decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Atazanavir and Modafinil: Atazanavir increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat and Modafinil: Cobicistat increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Atazanavir and Pemigatinib: Atazanavir increases pemigatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Cobicistat and Perampanel: Cobicistat increases perampanel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. These interactions highlight the importance of careful consideration when prescribing or co-administering drugs that affect CYP3A4 metabolism. Always consult detailed drug monographs for specific dosage adjustments and recommendations.
